purpose: Teach: ヒール/ハザード/聖職/刺繍/中心地/辿っ/オートバイ/マンゴー

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖母ちゃん、絶対、ハイヒール、絶対、履いてたわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, Granny wore those high heels all the time, remember? You do remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Warm, nostalgic opening. Soft rhythm like a memory being gently turned over. Reaching toward her with tenderness in the voice. Seeks confirmation like he's checking that she was there too.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。昔の車、本気で、絶対、ハザードランプ、絶対、なかった時代、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes. Those old cars, back when they didn't even have hazard lights, you remember that time, don't you?
lines.style: Joining him in the reverie. Gentle, almost dreamy pacing. She's not answering him so much as adding her own layer to the memory. Quiet delight underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、教会の聖職者、絶対、結婚式を、絶対、執り行ってくださったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で、絶対、感謝、本気、絶対、本気で。
lines.en: Back then, the priest at the church—he actually performed our wedding ceremony. You remember that, don't you? I'm grateful for it. Really grateful.
lines.style: Voice softens on the memory of the ceremony. Unhurried, honoring the moment. Gratitude lands with quiet weight, not performed but genuinely felt. Slight pause before the last statement of gratitude.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、私、絶対、刺繍、絶対、得意だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で、絶対、思い出
lines.en: When you were young, I was quite good at embroidery, remember? You do remember, don't you? Those memories…
lines.style: Gentle pride in a small skill once held. Nostalgic but not mournful. She's offering him a piece of who she was. Trails off slightly, letting the memory settle rather than finish it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、東京の中心地に、絶対、二人で、絶対、よく、絶対、行ったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で、絶対、思い出、本気、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: In those days, we used to go to the heart of Tokyo so often, just the two of us. You remember that, don't you? Those were real memories.
lines.style: Tender and specific. The rhythm is unhurried—he's savoring the detail of "just the two of us." Voice carries the weight of a precious shared past. Affirms it like it matters that she knows he still holds it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、戦争の道、絶対、辿った旅、絶対、語ってくれたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で、絶対、本気、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: When you were young, your father—he told us about the journey he took, the path the war had taken him. You remember him telling us that, don't you?
lines.style: Respectful, honoring the weight of what her father carried. Slower pace. There's reverence here for his story. Voice doesn't add drama—just lets the gravity of his words speak. Almost listening to the memory as she speaks.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、私、絶対、オートバイ、絶対、よく、絶対、乗ったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で、絶対、ロマンチック、絶対、本気、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: Back in those days, I rode my motorcycle quite often. Remember that? There was something romantic about it, really.
lines.style: A hint of boyish pride breaking through the nostalgia. The word "motorcycle" carries a small sparkle—he's remembering how it felt. Wistful but with an edge of wonder. Trails off gently on the last part.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、マンゴー、絶対、初めて、絶対、食べた日、覚えてる、あなた?本気で、絶対、感動した
lines.en: When you were young, the day I first ate mango—do you remember that? I was so moved by it.
lines.style: Soft wonder in the voice. The memory of that first taste still delights her. Simple, uncomplicated joy. Closes gently, like she's savoring the feeling of it again.
